about: 10CL016 per-register FF control bits (offline, Quartus builds of xdev design ffe2: with dffeas primitives). Cells relative to the LAB: frame = LUT frame 0 of LE N0 + 11, byte = low LUT byte of LE N0 + offset, plane = LE N0's LUT plane. sync_enable[i] (frame +11): set iff the register of LE i uses the LAB's synchronous clear/load (the same bit for sclr and sload, additive 15/15 each; LAB-wide bits choose clear vs load). aclr_enable[i] (frame +10): set iff it uses the LAB's asynchronous-clear line (additive 15/15, identical at X10Y10 and X22Y8). pair_select[i]: selects which of the LAB's two clock-enable lines the register of LE i uses; Quartus always keeps the lowest-numbered register on line 0, so the bit for LEs 0, 4, 8, 12 was not observed (null). Identical at X10Y10, X22Y8, X30Y20 for LEs 0-3 (16/16 combinations each); LEs 4-15 from X10Y10 only. Driving the LAB-wide lines needs routing bits, not mapped here. Not tested on silicon. pair_select_predicted: the 12 observed select bits sit in exactly the aclr_enable byte columns (frame +11 instead of +10), so the 4 unobserved ones are predicted there. Byte wrap: if low byte + offset < 1, use plane + 1 and byte + 252 (+251 if the new plane is >= 5); this threshold (1, unlike the LUT cells' 2) was fitted after the blind test below. Blind test at X6Y12, X28Y5, X19Y22 (18 random cases): 16/18 as predicted; the 2 misses were wrap cases at X19Y22, and with the wrap 18/18. Clock: a register clocked by a different signal flips the same pair_select bit (ffe2:clk, 16/16 combinations at X10Y10 and X22Y8), so the bit selects one of the LAB's two {clock, clock-enable} pairs.

lab_wide.about: [frame offset, byte offset] relative to LE N0's LUT frame 0 / low byte, LUT plane; bits present at all 5 LABs (X10Y10, X22Y8, X30Y20, X6Y12, X28Y5) when a control signal C (pin) drives the given register controls (ffe2 builds). The remaining 0-14 bits per LAB vary and are the routing of C onto a control line. Meanings are inferred. second_pair_used appears whenever the registers split across the two {clock, enable} pairs (ena K=1, clk K=1). sload_used includes it too (sload routes asdata = A); clock_all_on_C is the clock line's source change when every register moves from clock B to C.
